decisions.reason: As a flagship service close to the core vessel-management business in a growing industry and within an expanding large firm, it is likely to meet or stay near aspirations and is supported by enough organisational slack to retain it.

This service directly extends the firm's established crew and corporate support offer, so its fit with existing customers and capabilities makes management more likely to keep it unless results clearly disappoint.

Although the digital portal is somewhat more uncertain than traditional services, it was presented as a strategic focus and supports broader, more integrated customer service, which lowers the chance of withdrawal in an expanding firm.

The mobile performance app is the most experimental and easiest to reallocate resources away from if uptake falls short of aspirations, but the firm's growth, size, and strategic move toward broader service offerings still make retention slightly more likely than exit.
